Welcome
Welcome to our wonderful Gold Rights Respecting school! I am extremely proud to be the Chief Executive Officer of Haymoor Junior School and I am passionate about everyone doing their very best for this much-loved school.
Haymoor Junior School is a member of the TEACH Poole Trust - The Educational Alliance Of Canford Heath - which oversees not only Haymoor Junior School, but also Canford Heath Junior School, Canford Heath Infant School and Ad Astra Infant School. Through leading all four schools and ensuring we all work together, we are able to get the best from each one, to ensure your child has the very best primary school experience possible.
I hope that the information on our website is useful to you and that you can find everything you need to know. But please do not hesitate to contact myself or the Headteacher, Lucy Waterhouse, if we can help in any way.
We look forward to working with your child, yourself and your family. We will work together to make your child’s school life as meaningful and enjoyable as possible and prepare them for secondary school and beyond.

Curriculum (including Music and Sport)
Here at Haymoor Junior School, we provide an engaging, motivating and meaningful curriculum that is inspiring to all our children and provides the very best start for them. Subjects are, where possible, integrated into exciting themed topics and learning activities which provide a carefully sequenced progression of skills, development and knowledge. Children themselves contribute to curriculum design and their feedback is often used to help update and improve our children’s learning experiences.

Safeguarding, SEND & Pastoral
Safeguarding
At Haymoor Junior School, safeguarding is of the utmost importance. The school aims to help protect the children in its care by working consistently and appropriately with all agencies to reduce risk and promote the welfare of children.
If you have any concerns regarding the safety of a child, please contact our Designated Safeguarding Lead, Miss Hooker, or our Deputy Safeguarding Lead, Mrs Killahena.
Special Educational Needs & Disabilities (SEND)
We pride ourselves on providing inclusive schools with a range of expertise in supporting a wide variety of needs. We are committed to valuing all children equally and believing that all children are entitled to a relevant curriculum that is differentiated to meet their individual needs. We aim to identify children experiencing difficulties as early as possible and ensure that appropriate educational provision is made for them. We work very closely with a wide range of outside agencies and in close partnership with parents to support any child who may need additional support. Children with SEND are included in all aspects of the school curriculum, with their peer group.

Music
“Music gives soul to the universe, wings to the mind, flight to the imagination and life to everything.” Article 29: Your education should help you use and develop your talents and abilities.
Creativity is at the core of everything we do in the music department and we aim to inspire our pupils to develop a love of music through listening, composing, appraising, performing, singing and playing musical instruments. We are very fortunate to have a specialist music room, which is well equipped to accommodate weekly curriculum lessons.
We take part in many musical adventures. We are very fortunate to work closely with the BSO and SoundStorm and take part in many projects with them, such as The Royal Albert Hall and Symphony 125. The whole school takes part in Christmas concerts at our local churches every December and our choirs sing at the church lunch events. We work alongside our community on many occasions, such as, Canford Heath Fest, Carols by Torchlight and our Senior Citizen Cream Tea. Every year 500 children take part in our TEACH Trust Summer Concert that takes place at the Lighthouse, where we perform to a sold out concert hall.
